name: IEC integrator element (∫)
summary: Analogue element marked with an integral sign; the output is proportional to the time integral of the input.
description: The integrator element shows the integral sign inside a rectangular analogue element, usually with an amplifier mark. Its output changes at a rate proportional to the input, so a constant input produces a ramp. Reset or initial-condition inputs may be added to set the starting value.

Integrators appear in PI controllers, ramp generators and charge measurement. On the drawing, the time constant and any reset arrangement should be stated, because without them the element can drift to saturation.
The element does not specify the realisation. An op-amp with a feedback capacitor is common, but digital integration in a controller is drawn the same way on functional diagrams.
readingNotes: Look for a reset or initial condition input.
Find the time constant in notes or component values.
drawingChecklist: Reference the implementing circuit or function block.
distinction: The differentiator element uses d/dt and responds to rate of change rather than accumulated value.
